title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): A is a commutative Dedekind domain with fraction field K. An A-preadditive category C is called a 'catégorie de Deuring' if some object X satisfies three conditions. (a) O = End(X) is a maximal order in the central simple (Azumaya) K-algebra E = O⊗_A K. (b) For every rank-1 projective right O-module P, the object P⊗_O X exists in C. (c) P ↦ P⊗_O X is an equivalence between rank-1 projective right O-modules and C.

The model to keep in mind is the category of supersingular elliptic curves over F_p-bar with Z-module Hom groups (the Deuring correspondence). This is presumably why the notion sits in notes on a 'Galois theory of motives'.

Step 1 (top of page). This finishes the proof that the condition does not depend on the choice of X. Take C = P(O) and an object P with O' = End_O(P). The functor Q ↦ Q⊗_{O'} P has a quasi-inverse P' ↦ Hom_C(P,P'). Here Hom_C(P,P') is viewed as a right O'-module via the action of O' on P. This is standard Morita theory restricted to invertible modules.

Step 2: classification of such categories by algebras.
- C is determined up to non-canonical A-linear equivalence by the A-algebra O = End(X). A marginal addition says every A-algebra O defines such a category P(O), the right O-modules locally free of rank 1.
- Claim: P(O) ≃ P(O') A-linearly iff there is an (O,O')-bimodule L that is projective of rank 1 over O and over O'. One takes L = F(O) for an equivalence F. This relation is an equivalence relation.
- Consequence: equivalent orders have isomorphic generic algebras, O⊗K ≅ O'⊗K.
- Converse, for maximal orders in central simple algebras (called 'well known'): embed both in the same E. A crossed-out first attempt used L = {x ∈ E : xO ⊂ O'x}. The final choice is the product L = O·O' = {Σ λ_i μ_i}, which lies in E (the page writes ⊂ K). Because O and O' are maximal, this connecting bimodule is invertible.

Step 3: maximality is preserved under equivalence. If O is maximal in O⊗K and O' is equivalent to O, then O' is maximal. The argument continues on the next page: maximality is local, and O, O' are locally isomorphic since a rank-1 projective is locally free.

Where this leads (next page):
- Equivalence classes of 'strictly Dieudonné' categories are matched with central simple algebras, i.e. with Br(K).
- Equivalences between two such categories form a 'torsor category' under the auto-equivalences.
- These auto-equivalences are described by invertible O-bimodules, whose automorphisms of the identity functor are given by the centre.
errors: The criterion 'there exists a bimodule L projective of rank 1 over O and over O′' is not sufficient in general. One also needs O′ → End_O(L) (and O → End_{O′}(L)) to be isomorphisms, i.e. L must be an invertible bimodule. For maximal orders this holds automatically: End_O(L) is an order containing O′, hence equal to it. Grothendieck does not state this.
The product O·O′ lies in E (the common K-algebra), not in K as written.

The converse depends on O and O′ being maximal orders in the same (isomorphic) central simple algebra. The local input (all maximal orders over a DVR, or its completion, are conjugate) is invoked only as 'bien connu'.

Next page: classes of categories are matched with Br(K). The invariant actually obtained is the isomorphism class of the central simple algebra E. E and M_n(E) give inequivalent categories but the same Brauer class, so 'Br(K)' is correct only up to this, unless 'strictement Dieudonnéen' imposes extra conditions (e.g. E a division algebra).

ideas.what: Quasi-inverse P′ ↦ Hom_C(P,P′) to Q ↦ Q⊗_{O′}P between categories of rank-1 projective modules
ideas.modern_name: Morita equivalence restricted to invertible modules (Picard groupoid level)

ideas.what: A-linear equivalence P(O) ≃ P(O′) iff there is an invertible (O,O′)-bimodule
ideas.modern_name: Morita equivalence / invertible bimodules (Picard groupoid of orders)

ideas.what: Two maximal orders in the same central simple algebra over a Dedekind ring are connected by the invertible bimodule O·O′, and maximality is a local property
ideas.modern_name: Connecting ideals of maximal orders; local conjugacy of maximal orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring, Eichler; Auslander–Goldman (1960); Reiner, Maximal Orders

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatization of 'Deuring categories': A-linear categories equivalent to rank-1 projectives over a maximal order, classified by the generic central simple algebra
ideas.modern_name: Categorical Deuring correspondence (supersingular elliptic curves ↔ invertible right modules over a maximal quaternion order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941) for the correspondence; categorical form in recent expositions (e.g. Voight's Quaternion Algebras)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck formulated an intrinsic, choice-free characterization of 'Deuring categories'. These are A-linear categories classified up to equivalence by the generic central simple algebra of a maximal order. They are clearly meant as models for categories of motives such as supersingular elliptic curves. Later expositions present the categorical Deuring correspondence without this abstract framing or any attribution to him. The page itself contains only standard Morita and maximal-order facts.
missed.quote: La catégorie C est connue à équivalence (non canonique) près quand on connaît une A-algèbre O = End(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It documents an early categorical view of the Deuring correspondence inside Grothendieck's motivic Galois theory, which is relevant to current work on categorical/supersingular isogeny equivalences. No new theorem is involved.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is classical Morita theory plus well-known facts on maximal orders, which Grothendieck himself calls 'bien connu'. The only mildly interesting aspect is the historical framing: axiomatizing Deuring-type categories within the 1965 motivic Galois project.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed as 'σ' throughout is Grothendieck's script 𝒪 (the order O), consistent with the previous and next pages.
'σ.σ′ = {Σ λ_i μ_i} ⊂ K': the product should lie in E (the bold letter may be E). It must sit in the common algebra E, not in K.

Margin note: likely 'Toute A-algèbre 𝒪 définit une catégorie de Deuring (P(𝒪) = cat. des 𝒪-modules à droite loc. libres de rang 1)', i.e. 'de Deuring' rather than 'de Morita' and 'rang 1' rather than 'rang fini'.
'{+(à g.)+}' near 'qui commute' appears to read '(cf. g.)' or '(à g.)'. It is uncertain.
